details: CONFIRMED by replay. The guard is a safety check: it should not let a run start that will pass the day's cap.
The largest stored batch was conservative except when the suite grew; the per-case sum is a central estimate
(each case at its newest cost), so it is below the actual cost about half the time. Replay over the 20 stored full
batches (records before each one, its own case list): new < actual in 10 of 20 (worst: 27 Oct 07-35 by $4.36,
28 Oct 07-10 by $1.93); old < actual in 5 of 20, all of them suite growth or a new maximum. max(old, new) is below
actual in 3 of 20 (16-45 23 Oct, 16-31 24 Oct, 07-35 27 Oct). So the change fixes suite growth but loosens the guard
for every run where the newest batch was cheaper than the largest; SUITE_MARGIN's own comment measures failing runs
at 1.57x the green ones. The fix hint of the earlier review ("per-case when it exists, else the largest batch")
was followed literally; taking the larger of the two keeps both protections. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: python3 bin/paid-cost guard eval --today 2026-10-26 --dir <copy before 01-47-23Z> --repo <27 cases>, spent 188:
branch: "... this run is estimated at $17.39 ..." rc=1; master: "... estimated at $15.03 ..." rc=1; spent 170: rc=0

failing_case: Real records in ~/.relay/evals/relay before 2026-10-28T07-10-29Z, the 31 cases of that run, $19.00 left of the
day's cap. Now: the guard estimates $17.87 (each case at its newest stored cost) and lets the run start; it cost
$19.80, so the --within-day ceiling stops it part-way, the very harm the item set out to remove. Master estimated
$21.41 (largest batch) and refused it. Should: refuse (an estimate of at least $21.41).

(home is None in production, the same root default_dir reads); add a test with a stored expensive batch and a
cheaper newest batch of the same cases, no growth, where the room lies between them: refused.
